layers.message: Move to Node 22 and rename test script to test:unit
Start cycle for built-in Set methods

graderOnly: The committed .standards/CONTEXT.md says the runtime is Node.js 20 (.nvmrc 20, engines >=20) and that the test command is `npm test`; current package.json (engines.node >=22, only a `test:unit` script), .nvmrc (22), .github/workflows/ci.yml (`npm run test:unit`, Node version from .nvmrc), and README establish Node.js 22 and `npm run test:unit`. `npm test` now fails with a missing-script error.

The CONTEXT.md Evidence line citing `npm test` with 7 passing tests and the Testing line saying test files are listed in the `test` script are part of the same stale command claim; the unit suite now has 10 tests run by `npm run test:unit`.

Everything else in CONTEXT.md (library purpose, ES modules, no dependencies, src/index.js, src/tags.js, src/notes.js boundaries, conventions, test framework, existing helper behavior) is accurate for the current repository.
The active request (replace hand-written set helpers with built-in Set methods, which need Node 22, and keep the tests passing) depends on the runtime version and the test command.
The Node 22 move was an ordinary committed change made after the previous cycle was signed off; it is established baseline, not cycle residue (BaselineReconciliation is NONE).
The correct outcome is a gap-fill refresh of CONTEXT.md followed by a FORWARD handoff AUDITING -> SCOPING with a /scoper invocation.

all.why: the stale claims must be corrected in the context file
the verified test command is the exact script name
the verified runtime version appears in the refreshed context
the still-accurate, cycle-relevant module boundary is preserved
the still-accurate module boundary that uses the helpers is preserved
exactly one Project Context document, not an appended second copy

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Auditor does not mutate project artifacts to learn about them (this also catches a package-lock.json created by npm install)
Auditor creates or edits no cycle records; earlier cycle records are preserved

selfChecks.why: the current test command established by package.json works and the suite passes
the command recorded in the stale context no longer exists

selfChecks.cmd: node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); if (p.engines.node !== '>=22' || p.scripts.test || !p.scripts['test:unit']) process.exit(1)" && grep -qx 22 .nvmrc && grep -q 'npm run test:unit' .github/workflows/ci.yml
selfChecks.why: manifests and scripts establish Node 22 and test:unit
the committed context still describes Node 20 and npm test
the built-in Set methods the cycle depends on exist on the project runtime

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 00-project (pre-install): dependency-free ES-module library `taglist` on Node 20 with `npm test`, .nvmrc 20, CI using .nvmrc and `npm test`. Installer runs. 10-all-tags-filter: a previous STANDARD cycle (${PRIOR}) squashed into one commit: its Auditor-written .standards/CONTEXT.md (Node.js 20, `npm test`, 7 tests), complete scope/spec/plan/verification/both reviews/documentation/synchronization records, the notesWithAllTags code and tests, README entry, and STATE.md SIGNED_OFF. 20-node-22: ordinary post-sign-off commit moving to Node 22 (engines >=22, .nvmrc 22) and renaming the only test script to `test:unit` (CI and README updated); nothing else the context describes changes. 30-cycle: STATE.md starts the new STANDARD cycle ${ID} at AUDITING with Handoff NEW_CYCLE from SIGNED_OFF, AuditTarget NONE, recovery inactive, BaselineReconciliation NONE. The request (replace hand-written set helpers with built-in Set methods, keep tests passing) depends on Node 22 and the test command. CONTEXT.md is generic about notes.js filters so it stays accurate after the prior cycle's addition; only runtime and test-command claims are stale.
